title: Understanding fractions
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

sections.title: Name a fraction from a picture
sections.objective: Say what fraction of a bar, a rectangle or a group is shaded.
explain: The bottom number of a fraction (the denominator) is how many equal parts make the whole. The top number (the numerator) is how many of those parts you're talking about.
So to name a shaded fraction: count all the equal parts for the bottom, and count the shaded parts for the top. 3 shaded parts out of 5 equal parts is {3/5}.
Compare the shaded parts to ALL the parts, not to the unshaded ones. 3 shaded and 2 not shaded is {3/5}, not {3/2}.

sections.title: Fractions on a number line
sections.objective: Read a fraction from a number line, including fractions bigger than 1.
explain: On a number line, the whole is the distance from 0 to 1. Count how many equal spaces it's cut into: that's the bottom number. Count the spaces, not the tick marks.
Then count spaces from 0 to the dot: that's the top number. A dot 3 spaces along, with the whole cut into 4 spaces, is at {3/4}.
Keep counting past 1 the same way. 5 spaces of fourths is {5/4}, which is also {1 1/4}: one whole and one more fourth. Each whole is cut the same way, so the bottom number stays 4.

sections.title: Fractions are division
sections.objective: Write a division as a fraction, and spot fractions that are whole numbers.
explain: The fraction bar means divide. 3 ÷ 4 = {3/4}: if 3 pizzas are shared equally by 4 people, each person gets {3/4} of a pizza. The number being divided goes on top.
When the top divides evenly by the bottom, the fraction is a whole number. {12/4} = 12 ÷ 4 = 3, and {6/6} = 1.
When the top is bigger and doesn't divide evenly, the answer is more than 1: 7 ÷ 3 = {7/3}, which is {2 1/3}.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Pictures, number lines and division, mixed together.
explain: Now the problems are mixed. In every one, ask: what is the whole, and how many equal parts is it cut into? That's the bottom number.
Then count the parts you need for the top number. For division, the number being divided goes on top.

hints.frac.meaning.read-models: Count ALL the equal parts for the bottom number. Count the shaded parts for the top number.
hints.frac.meaning.number-line: Count the spaces between 0 and 1 (not the marks): that's the bottom. Count spaces from 0 to the dot: that's the top.
hints.frac.meaning.division: The fraction bar means divide. The number being divided goes on top.
hints.frac.meaning: What's the whole, and how many equal parts is it cut into? That's the bottom number.

simplifyHint: That's the right amount, but it can be simpler. Does the bottom divide evenly into the top?

misconceptionMessages.frac.model-part-to-part: Compare the shaded parts to ALL the parts, not just the unshaded ones. The bottom number is how many parts there are in total.
misconceptionMessages.frac.model-unshaded: That's the part that isn't shaded. The question asks about the shaded part.
misconceptionMessages.frac.nl-counted-ticks: Count the spaces between 0 and 1, not the tick marks. There's always one more mark than there are spaces.
misconceptionMessages.frac.nl-whole-line: The whole is from 0 to 1, not the whole line. How many spaces are between 0 and 1?
misconceptionMessages.frac.division-flipped: Upside down: the number being divided goes on top. 3 ÷ 4 is {3/4}.
misconceptionMessages.frac.whole-subtracted: The fraction bar means divide, not subtract. How many times does the bottom go into the top?
